text:
Mira (infra): Heads-up — planning a synthetic admission probe in us-west-2 to validate our backpressure thresholds. Goal: exercise admission queueing when GPU pools hit ~85% so we can tune threshold+max-inflight. 30m window: 10m ramp, 10m sustain, 10m cool-down. Need someone to run loadgen and someone to watch metrics + abort if tails explode. Who's available at 13:00 PT?

Devin: I can run the generator. Which config do you want? want to test both KV-cached and cold paths?

Mira (infra): Yes — run two passes: `kv-hit=0.6` then `kv-hit=0.2`. Use the admission target mode so we hit admission controller directly. Example command:```bash
rloadgen --mode admission --qps 1200 --clients 40 --duration 1800 
  --kv-hit 0.6 --seq-dist p50=64,p95=512 
  --region us-west-2 --tag probe/admission-cal-1
```Start first at 13:00, give me +5s on the deploy so we can open dashboards.

Sahil: I'll watch `admission_queue.depth`, `admission.reject_rate`, `gpu_utilization` and tail latencies on `serve.p95`. Abort criterion: p95 serve latency > 30s OR sustained reject_rate > 15% for 2 consecutive mins. I'll also attach a temporary alert.

Jen: Also recommend simulating some network egress constraints for the probe (we saw last time a clean network made admission look fine). Use `tcq` on loadgen hosts or run a small proxy with `netem` so we can test cross-region spillover behavior.

loadgen-bot: starting run (tag=probe/admission-cal-1) at ts=1842109876, ramp plan=10m->hold->cooldown. Reporting to #eng-infra.

Devin: First pass (kv-hit=0.6) observations: ramped to target. At ~84% GPU util we started to see 429 rejects from admission controller. serve.p95 jumped from ~120ms -> ~480ms. admission_queue.depth peaked at ~450. Dumped logs to s3://redwood-test-logs/admission/probe1/ and /tmp/admission-probe-1.log.

Mira (infra): Good data. Let's try lowering admission threshold to 0.8 and rerun same load to see if earlier rejection avoids tail amplification. Current admission config we used for probe:```yaml
admission:
  threshold: 0.9
  max_inflight: 200
  overflow_policy: fallback_to_smaller_model
```
Change to:```yaml
admission:
  threshold: 0.8
  max_inflight: 160
```
Keep overflow_policy the same.

Sahil: After rerun with threshold=0.8 we saw fewer 429s but more fallback-model calls (503->fallback). Tail p95 reduced to ~300ms but cost per request increased ~22% due to fallbacks. Also note `kvcache.hit_rate` dropped slightly during sustained traffic which amplified CPU on CPU-bound routing pods.

Jen: If we enable cross-region spillover to eu-west-1, we saw earlier that tail improves but network egress increases. Suggest a staged rollback: set threshold=0.82 and enable spillover with a small weight (10%) and canary for 30m. I'll open PR for the config change + rollout doc.

Mira (infra): Agreed. Action items: 1) Jen opens PR with rollout/canary plan (target 0.82 + 10% spillover) 2) Dev runs one more verification pass with `kv-hit=0.2` to validate cold paths 3) Sahil tunes alerts to trigger earlier (reject_rate > 10% for 1m) 4) I'll update runbook note about tradeoff: lower threshold reduces tail but increases fallback cost.

Devin: Starting second pass (kv-hit=0.2) in ~5m. Will push logs and short summary to thread.

kube-bot: admission-controller configmap updated in staging (not prod) for testing.

Devin: Second pass results: cold KV made GPU load spikier; we hit the new threshold behavior early and saw a lot more fallbacks than first pass. p95 serve ~420ms, fallback rate ~18%. Uploading graphs to https://dash.redwood.company/d/abcd/admission-probe (private).

Mira (infra): Thanks everyone. Summary for the run: default threshold 0.9 is too permissive for current packing in us-west-2 -> leads to queue length growth and tail amplification. Recommended immediate change: threshold=0.82 + enable 10% cross-region spillover as a safety valve. Jen, please file PR and include the exact loadgen config + abort criteria we used. We'll schedule a controlled rollout tomorrow 09:30 PT with on-call coverage. :thumbsup:
